methodology_other: A deep learning model was trained to determine the footprints of buildings from high resolution satellite imagery. An accompanying [technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12283) describes the methodology used to generate the first version of the dataset. Further improvements were made for the subsequent versions, v2 and v3.
name: buildings-google-cod
notes:
This large-scale open dataset consists of outlines of buildings derived from high-resolution 50 cm satellite imagery. It contains 1.8B building detections in Africa, Latin America, Caribbean, South Asia and Southeast Asia. The inference spanned an area of 58M km² and was carried out during May 2023.  
  

Each building in this dataset includes a polygon describing its footprint size on the ground and a confidence score indicating how sure this is a building. There is no information about the type of building, its street address, or any details other than its geometry.  
  

The HDX team curates these datasets at [Google Open Buildings (by HDX)](https://data.humdata.org/organization/google-open-buildings) using international boundaries from the UN Geospatial Hub.  
  

For more details, see the official website of the [Open Buildings dataset](https://sites.research.google/gr/open-buildings/).

organization.description:
Google Open Buildings is a large-scale open dataset of building footprints to support social good applications, from population estimation, urban planning and humanitarian response, to environmental and climate science.

The datasets on Google Open Buildings (by HDX) are curated by the HDX team and are published by country to better enable humanitarian response use. The HDX team uses international boundaries from the UN Geospatial Hub.
